questions.question: Why was public authentication postponed in May?
questions.expected_answer_summary: Public authentication was postponed from Q3 to Q4 because the authorization audit trail was incomplete and could not prove who changed permissions or when.

expected_claims.text: The public authentication rollout was postponed from Q3 to Q4 2026.
The reason was an incomplete authorization audit trail that could not prove who changed permissions or when.

expected_passages.quote: The public authentication rollout is postponed from Q3 to Q4 2026.
The authorization audit trail is incomplete

questions.question: Who approved the May authentication postponement, and who owned readiness?
questions.expected_answer_summary: Elena Park approved the postponement, and Priya Nair owned authentication readiness.

expected_claims.text: Elena Park approved the May 20 authentication postponement.
Priya Nair owned authentication readiness.

expected_passages.quote: Elena Park approved the postponement on May 20, 2026, and Priya Nair owns authentication readiness.

questions.question: What authentication change was proposed in June, when would it start, and who owned it?
questions.expected_answer_summary: The June proposal was an employee-only OpenID Connect beta starting July 15, owned by Priya Nair.

expected_claims.text: The June proposal was an employee-only authentication beta using the existing OpenID Connect provider.
It was proposed to start July 15, 2026.
Priya Nair was the decision owner.

expected_passages.quote: Start an employee-only authentication beta on July 15, 2026, using the existing OpenID Connect provider.

questions.question: Was the June authentication proposal later changed, and did that change release public authentication?
questions.expected_answer_summary: Yes. The July decision moved the internal beta from July 15 to July 22 and superseded the June proposal, but public rollout remained postponed to Q4.

expected_claims.text: The July decision moved the internal beta from July 15 to July 22 and superseded the June proposal.
The July revision was only for the internal beta; the public rollout remained postponed to Q4.

expected_passages.quote: This accepted revision supersedes the June 12 proposal to begin the internal beta on July 15.
Public customer authentication remains postponed to Q4 2026.

questions.question: Who owns the July internal authentication beta and who owns its security approval?
questions.expected_answer_summary: Priya Nair owns the rollout, while Jonah Reed owns security approval.

expected_claims.text: Priya Nair owns the July internal-beta rollout.
Jonah Reed owns security approval.

expected_passages.quote: Priya Nair owns the rollout, and Jonah Reed owns security approval.

questions.question: Why did the internal authentication beta move from July 15 to July 22?
questions.expected_answer_summary: It moved one week so all six authorization audit events could complete integration testing; the permission-override replay test was still failing.

expected_claims.text: The beta moved one week so all six authorization audit events could complete integration testing.
The permission-override event still failed the replay test.

expected_passages.quote: The date moved by one week so all six authorization audit events can complete integration testing.
the permission-override event still fails the replay test.

questions.question: What must Atlas record for every authorization change before authentication reaches customers?
questions.expected_answer_summary: Every role grant, removal, and permission override must record actor, subject, previous value, new value, and timestamp.

expected_claims.text: Role grants, role removals, and permission overrides must record actor, subject, previous value, new value, and timestamp.

expected_passages.quote: Every role grant, role removal, and permission override must record actor, subject, previous value, new value, and timestamp

questions.question: Did the team accept identity-provider login logs as sufficient authorization evidence?
questions.expected_answer_summary: No. That alternative was rejected because login logs do not capture application-level authorization changes.

expected_claims.text: Depending only on identity-provider login logs was rejected.
Those logs do not capture application-level authorization changes.

expected_passages.quote: Depend only on identity-provider login logs. Status: rejected.

questions.question: Who owns authentication according to the July records, and do the sources agree?
questions.expected_answer_summary: The approved July 8 memo names Priya Nair as rollout owner, but the July 18 planning note says Marco Silva. The sources conflict, and the planning note records no approval or security evidence.

expected_claims.text: The approved July 8 decision memo names Priya Nair as rollout owner.
The July 18 planning readout says Marco Silva owns the rollout.
The sources conflict, and the planning group recorded no approval or supporting security evidence for its statement.

expected_passages.quote: Priya Nair owns the rollout
Public authentication is active for Q3 and Marco Silva owns the rollout.

questions.question: Was public authentication active in Q3 after the July decisions, or was it still postponed?
questions.expected_answer_summary: The approved July 8 memo says public authentication remained postponed to Q4. A July 18 planning note claims it was active in Q3, but explicitly lacks approval and supporting security evidence, so the evidence conflicts.

expected_claims.text: The approved July 8 memo keeps public customer authentication postponed to Q4.
The July 18 planning note conflicts by claiming public authentication is active in Q3.
The planning note records no approval or supporting security evidence for that claim.

expected_passages.quote: Public customer authentication remains postponed to Q4 2026.
This statement conflicts with the approved July 8 decision memo

questions.question: Why was building password authentication rejected for the internal beta?
questions.expected_answer_summary: It was rejected because Atlas would assume new credential-storage responsibility.

expected_claims.text: Building password authentication was rejected because it would create new credential-storage responsibility.

expected_passages.quote: The team rejected password authentication because it would create new credential-storage responsibility.

questions.question: Which search technologies did Atlas choose for the MVP, and why?
questions.expected_answer_summary: Atlas chose PostgreSQL full-text search and pgvector in one primary database to simplify local installation and support transactional version retirement.

expected_claims.text: PostgreSQL full-text search and pgvector will share the primary MVP database.
The reason was simpler local installation and transactional document-version retirement.

expected_passages.quote: PostgreSQL full-text search and pgvector will share the primary database for the MVP.
One database keeps local installation simple and supports transactional document-version retirement.

questions.question: What was decided about Slack, Notion, and Google Drive connectors?
questions.expected_answer_summary: Those connectors were postponed until after the local-file MVP so evidence quality could first be established for Markdown, text, DOCX, and PDF.

expected_claims.text: Slack, Notion, and Google Drive connectors were postponed until after the local-file MVP.
The team wanted to establish evidence quality for Markdown, text, DOCX, and PDF first.

expected_passages.quote: Slack, Notion, and Google Drive connectors are postponed until after the local-file MVP.
establish evidence quality on Markdown, text, DOCX, and PDF

questions.question: What passage chunk size did the architecture team settle on?
questions.expected_answer_summary: It did not settle a final size. The team proposed experiments near 500 tokens and required benchmark evidence before fixing the value.

expected_claims.text: Chunks near 500 tokens were proposed as an experimental starting point.
No final chunk size was fixed because benchmark evidence was still needed.

expected_passages.quote: Begin retrieval experiments with chunks near 500 tokens and preserve source boundaries.
The team needs benchmark evidence before fixing a final chunk size.

questions.question: Will Ollama model weights be bundled in the application images?
questions.expected_answer_summary: No. Atlas decided not to bundle model weights because they change independently and would make images too large; installation uses an explicit model-pull step.

expected_claims.text: Ollama model weights will not be bundled in application images.
Model installation will use an explicit pull step because weights change independently and would make images too large.

expected_passages.quote: Do not bundle Ollama model weights in the application images.
Installation will use an explicit model-pull step.

questions.question: What retrieval target defines success for the Atlas benchmark?
questions.expected_answer_summary: The expected source must appear in the top five results for at least 80 percent of answerable benchmark questions.

expected_claims.text: The expected source must rank in the top five for at least 80 percent of answerable benchmark questions.

expected_passages.quote: The expected source must appear in the top five retrieval results for at least 80 percent
